intro: Learn the reflexive verbs used for washing and daily personal care.
b1.texto:
Reflexive verbs take reflexive pronouns that agree with the subject:

- **yo me** ducho / lavo
- **tú te** duchas / lavas
- **él/ella/usted se** ducha / lava
- **nosotros nos** duchamos / lavamos
- **vosotros os** ducháis / laváis
- **ellos/ustedes se** duchan / lavan

With parts of the body we use the definite article, not the possessive: *me lavo **las** manos*, *me lavo **los** dientes*.
b4.texto: Notice how the reflexive pronoun agrees with the subject of the sentence.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence shows an action done to oneself?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Exactly! Me lavo shows a reflexive action.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Lavo el coche shows an action done to an outside object.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Se lava refers to another person.
b7.pregunta: Choose the first person plural reflexive pronoun.
b8.traduccion: My brother goes to bed very late.
b9.pregunta: Translate into Spanish: «I go to bed late.»
p.me ducho.consejo: Washing yourself under the shower water.
p.me lavo.consejo: Cleaning your body or a part of it.
p.los dientes.consejo: The hard white pieces in your mouth.
p.el cepillo de dientes.consejo: A tool for cleaning your mouth and teeth.
p.el champú.consejo: Liquid soap for washing the hair.
p.el jabón.consejo: A substance for washing the body.
p.tarde.consejo: Past the usual time, or at the end of the day.
p.temprano.consejo: In the first hours of the morning.
p.las manos.consejo: The parts at the ends of your arms.
b2.f0.texto: What time do you usually get up?
b2.f1.texto: I get up at seven and take a shower.
b2.f2.texto: And what do you do afterwards in the bathroom?
b2.f3.texto: I get dressed and brush my teeth.
b2.f4.texto: My brother always goes to bed very late.
b2.f5.texto: He gets up at eleven, cheerful.
b4.e1.texto: She washes her hands with soap.
b5.f0.texto: Every morning I wake up full of energy when the sunlight comes in.
b5.f1.texto: I go to the bathroom and shower with mild shampoo and hot water.
b5.f2.texto: Afterwards I use the toothbrush to clean my mouth carefully.
b5.f3.texto: In front of the hallway mirror I comb my hair and shave slowly.
b5.f4.texto: In my bedroom I choose clean clothes and get dressed quickly to go out.
b5.f5.texto: At night I lie down in bed to rest from the whole day.
b8.frase: Mi hermano se acuesta muy tarde.
p.acuesta.consejo: From «acostarse»: the «o» turns into «ue» in «acuesta», «acuestas», «acuestan». The «se» goes before it.
p.lava.consejo: It is written with «v» but sounds like «b»: «LA-ba». «Se lava» means she washes herself.
p.sol.consejo: One short syllable, no accent mark: «sol». It belongs with «solar» and «soleado» (sunny).
p.champú.consejo: The Spanish spelling of «shampoo»: «cham-PU». The accent mark is on the last syllable.
p.suave.consejo: The «ua» is one sound: «SWA-be». The «v» is pronounced like a «b».
p.uso.consejo: From «usar». The «yo» form ends in «-o». Here it is a verb, not the noun «el uso».
p.lavarme.consejo: It is «lavar» with «me» attached at the end. «Me» means myself and is glued to the infinitive.
p.frente.consejo: Here it is used with «a»: «frente al espejo», in front of the mirror. As a noun, «la frente» is the forehead.
p.espejo.consejo: Mind the «j»: it sounds like an «h», so say «es-PE-ho». The plural is «espejos».
p.pasillo.consejo: The «ll» sounds like a «y»: «pa-SI-yo». It comes from «paso» (step), because you walk along it.
p.dormitorio.consejo: From «dormir» (to sleep): the room for sleeping. Stress «TO»: «dor-mi-TO-ryo».
p.elijo.consejo: From «elegir»: the «e» becomes «i» and the «g» becomes «j» before «-o». Say the «j» like an «h».
p.limpia.consejo: Stress the first syllable and say «ia» as one sound: «LIM-pya». The masculine form is «limpio».
p.levantamos.consejo: From «levantarse», to get up. The ending «-amos» means «nosotros», and «nos» goes before the verb.
p.se.consejo: A small word said without stress: «se». In «se acuesta», it shows the person puts themselves to bed.
